Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:1.hebrew: רבה אמר לעולם בטובח בעצמו ור' מאיר - בעלמא, בתשלומי ממון, לית ליה מת ומשלם, והכא תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה קנס הם, וכל משפט קנס חידוש הוא. הלכך, אע"ג דמיקטיל נמי, לא מיפטר מיניה. ולקמן פריך: לרבה אליבא דרבי מאיר קשיא — בתו דמתניתין נמי קנס הוא, וקא פטר ליה אבתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:1.english: Rabbah said: Actually, [we are dealing] with one who slaughters [it] himself, and Rabbi Meir - In general, regarding monetary payments, he does not hold [that one] dies and pays; here, however, the fourfold and fivefold payments are a fine, and every law of a fine is a novel ruling. Therefore, even though he is executed as well, he is not exempt from it. And later, [the Gemara] asks: According to Rabbah's view of Rabbi Meir, [this is] difficult — [the case of] his daughter in our Mishnah is also a fine, yet he exempts him on account of his daughter.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:2.hebrew: היה גדי גנוב לו - גנב גדי בחול ונתחייב הקרן, וטבחו בשבת, דלא אתי עליה חיובא דממון באיסור שבת אלא חיוב קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:2.english: [If] he had a stolen kid - He stole a kid on a weekday and became liable [for] the principal, and [then] slaughtered it on Shabbat, so that a monetary obligation does not come upon him together with the prohibition of Shabbat, [but] rather an obligation of a fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:3.hebrew: חייב - ד' וה', דקנס חידוש הוא, ורבה סבירא ליה כרבי מאיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:3.english: [He is] liable - [To pay] fourfold and fivefold [restitution], for a fine is a novel [ruling], and Rabbah holds like Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:4.english: He stole and slaughtered on Shabbat - For the monetary obligation of the principal came upon him with the prohibition of Shabbat.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:5.hebrew: פטור - דקיימא לן: אין מת ומשלם, וכיון דאקרן לא מיחייב, קנס נמי לא משלם, דתשלומי ד' וה' אמר רחמנא, ולא תשלומי שלשה וארבעה. ולא סבירא לן כרבי נתן, דאמר (שבת דף צד) חי נושא את עצמו, אי נמי בכפות:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:5.english: He is exempt - For we maintain [that] one does not die and pay; and since he is not liable for the principal, he does not pay the fine either, for the Merciful One said "a fourfold or fivefold payment," and not a threefold or fourfold payment. And we do not hold like Rabbi Natan, who said (Shabbat 94a) [that] a living creature carries itself; or else, [the case is] with a bound [animal].

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:6.hebrew: שאם אין גניבה - כלומר, שמאחר שפטור על הקרן משום מיתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:6.english: For if there is no theft - That is to say, since he is exempt from [paying] the principal because of [the] death [penalty].

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:7.hebrew: אין טביחה ואין מכירה - אינו מחויב קנס כדפירשתי, דתשלומי ארבעה וחמשה כתיב, ולא תשלומי שלשה וארבעה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:1:7.english: [There is] no slaughter and no sale - He is not obligated [to pay] a fine, as I have explained, for "a fourfold and fivefold payment" is written, and not "a threefold and fourfold payment."

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:2:1.english: Burglary - That he tunneled into a house and took it out.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:2:2.hebrew: וטבחו במחתרת - עצמה, דההיא שעתא בר קטלא הוא אי הוה אשכחיה בעל הבית, כדכתיב (שמות כב) אין לו דמים:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:2:2.english: And he slaughtered it in [the] burglary - [in the burglary] itself, for at that moment he is liable to be killed if the homeowner had found him, as it is written (Exodus 22[:1]), "there is no bloodguilt for him."

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:3:1.hebrew: משום דאסוריה איסור עולם - כל זמן שיעידו עליו שחילל שבת, ימיתוהו בית דין. הלכך, חמירא מיתה דילה לפוטרו מממון:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:3:1.english: Because its prohibition is an eternal prohibition - Whenever [witnesses] testify against him that he desecrated Shabbat, the court executes him; therefore, its death [penalty] is severe [enough] to exempt him from monetary [payment].

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:3:2.hebrew: דאיסור שעה - אי לא משכח ליה ההיא שעתא, תו לא מיקטיל:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:3:2.english: Which [is] a temporary prohibition - If [the homeowner] does not find him at that time, he is no longer killed.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:4:1.hebrew: היתה פרה שאולה לו וטבחה בשבת פטור - דההיא שעתא דקא טבח לה, גזיל לה ממרה, ומיתה וממון באין כאחד. ולא גרסינן "שאם אין גניבה אין טביחה ואין מכירה", דגבי שואל לא שייך לא כפל ולא ארבעה וחמשה, שהרי חייב בקרן לעולם, אפילו טוען טענת גנב; ואין קנס אלא או בגנב או בשומר חנם הפוטר עצמו בטוען טענת גנב, שאומר "נגנבה":
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:4:1.english: [If] a cow was lent to him and he slaughtered it on Shabbat, [he is] exempt - For at that [very] moment when he slaughters it, he steals it from its owner, and [thus] the death penalty and monetary [liability] come together. And we do not read [in the text]: "for if there is no theft, there is no slaughter and no sale," because regarding a borrower, neither double [payment] nor fourfold or fivefold [payment] applies, for he is always liable for the principal, even [if] he makes the claim of a thief; and a fine applies only either to a thief, or to an unpaid bailee who exempts himself by making the claim of a thief, saying, "It was stolen."

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:4:2.hebrew: פרה אתא לאשמועינן - בתמיה, מה למדנו ממנה שלא למדנו מגדי דקאמר רבה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:4:2.english: [Is] he coming to teach us [the case of] a cow - [Said] in astonishment: what did we learn from it that we did not learn from [the case of] a kid that Rabbah stated?

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:1.english: [A] borrowed [cow] he comes to teach us - That one who slaughters it on Shabbat is exempt.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:2.hebrew: ס"ד אמינא הואיל ואמר רב פפא - בהשוכר את הפועלים:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:2.english: It could enter your mind to say, since Rav Pappa said - In [the chapter entitled] HaSokher et HaPoalim.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:3.hebrew: הכא נמי - נימא משעת שאלה רמיא עליה חיוב קרן, וכי טבחה בשבת ליחייב:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:3.english: Here too - we would say [that] from the time of borrowing, the obligation of the principal rests upon him, and when he slaughters it on Shabbat, he should be liable.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:4.hebrew: קמ"ל - כיון דכל כמה דאיתא הדרא בעינא, ההיא שעתא דקא טבח לה קא גזיל לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:5:4.english: He teaches us - Since as long as it exists it returns as is, [at] that moment when he slaughters it, he is stealing it.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:6:1.english: All the days of its borrowing - All the days of the duration of the time that their father borrowed it from the owners.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:6:2.english: They are not liable for its unavoidable accident - For they are not borrowers with respect to it.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:6:3.hebrew: דמי בשר בזול - כל זוזא חשבינן בארבעה דנקי, הכי אמרינן בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב קמו:). והעור יחזירו לבעלים:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:6:3.english: The price of meat at a reduced [rate] - Every zuz we reckon at four dankei [two-thirds of a zuz]; so we say in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 146b). And the hide they return to the owners.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:1.hebrew: איכא דמתני ארישא - להאי הניח להן אביהן אחריות נכסים חייבין לשלם, ואמרינן דחייבין באונסין, דאישתעבוד נכסים דאבוהון מחיים משעת שאלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:1.english: Some teach [it] with regard to the first clause - [Referring] to this [statement]: "[If] their father left them property [as a] guarantee, they are liable to pay," and we say that they are liable for unavoidable accidents, since their father's property became encumbered during [his] lifetime from the time of the borrowing.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:2.hebrew: כ"ש אסיפא - כשטבחוה ואכלוה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:2.english: All the more so [with regard] to the latter clause - When they slaughtered it and ate it.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:3.hebrew: ופליגא דרב פפא - דאמר לעיל, ההיא שעתא דמטו לה אונסין הוא דאתי חיובא עליה, ולא משעת שאלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:3.english: And it disagrees with Rav Pappa - Who said above [that] at that moment when unavoidable accidents befall it, that is when liability comes upon him, and not from the time of borrowing.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:4.hebrew: ואיכא דמתני לה אסיפא - היכא דטבחוה, אם הניח להן אביהן אחריות נכסים, משלמין תשלומי מעליא ולא בזול, דאיבעי להו למידק:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:4.english: And some teach it with regard to the latter clause - Where they slaughtered it, if their father left them property as a guarantee, they pay full payment and not cheaply, because they should have investigated.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:5.hebrew: אבל ארישא - אם מתה, לא מיחייבי לשלומי, ולא אמרינן אישתעבוד נכסי דאבוהון משעת שאלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:5.english: However, with regard to the first clause - If it died, [the heirs] are not obligated to pay, and we do not say [that] their father's property became encumbered from the time of borrowing.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:6.hebrew: והיינו דרב פפא - דאמר לעיל לא אמרינן משעת שאלה רמו עליה תשלומין, אלא משעת אונסין ואילך, וההיא שעתא ליתיה לשואל דליחייב:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:7:6.english: And this is [the view] of Rav Pappa - Who said above [that] we do not say [that] from the time of borrowing, [liability for] payment is cast upon him, but rather from the time of the unavoidable accident and onward; and at that time, the borrower is not [alive] to become obligated.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:8:1.english: Granted, Rabbi Yochanan - who establishes our Mishnah as [referring to a case] where they did not forewarn him.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:8:2.hebrew: לא אמר כריש לקיש - דאוקמיה כר' מאיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:8:2.english: [He] did not say like Reish Lakish - Because he established it [the Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:8:3.english: When they did not forewarn him, [he is] exempt as well - Since there is an aspect of lashes.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:1.english: Unwittingly - That they did not forewarn them.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:2.hebrew: ודבר אחר - ממון. ואכולה מילתא קאי, כלומר: חייבי מיתות שוגגין וממון, או חייבי מלקיות שוגגין וממון:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:2.english: And another matter - Monetary [payment]. And it refers to the entire statement, that is to say: those liable to death [penalties] unwittingly and monetary [payment], or those liable to lashes unwittingly and monetary [payment].

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:3.hebrew: ר' יוחנן אומר חייב - בתשלומין:
Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:3.english: Rabbi Yochanan says [he is] liable - For [monetary] payment.

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:4.english: Since they did not forewarn him - and you only obligate him on account of one wickedness, [that] of monetary [payment].

Rashi on Ketubot 34b:9:5.english: When they did not forewarn him, [he is] exempt as well - And later [Ketubot 35a], [the Gemara] derives the reason.

Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:1:1.hebrew: ורבי מאיר לוקה ומשלם אית ליה מת ומשלם לית ליה ושאני הני - משמע דרבי מאיר אית ליה לוקה ומשלם אף בממון שאינו קנס, וכן משמע בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ צא.) שהבאתי לעיל. ותימה: דבפ"ק דמכות (ד' ד:) קאמר עולא טעמא דרבי מאיר דאמר עדים זוממין לוקין ומשלמין משום דגמר ממוציא שם רע, ופריך: מה למוציא שם רע שכן קנס? סבר לה כר' עקיבא דאמר עדים זוממין קנס הוא. משמע דבממון אינו לוקה ומשלם! ויש לומר: דודאי אי עדים זוממין הוי ממונא, לא הוה גמר ממוציא ש"ר שכן הוא קנס, אלא הוה דרשינן מ"כדי רשעתו" שאינו לוקה ומשלם. אבל השתא דסבר עדים זוממין קנסא, וגמר ממוציא שם רע דלוקין ומשלמין — ע"כ מוקי "כדי רשעתו" במיתה ומלקות. כיון ד"כדי רשעתו" לא הוי במלקות וממון, מהשתא בכל דוכתא לוקה ומשלם, דמהיכא נמעיט שלא ילקה וישלם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:1:1.english: "And Rabbi Meir holds that one is flogged and pays, [but] does not hold that one dies and pays; and these are different" - This implies that Rabbi Meir holds [that] one is flogged and pays even for monetary compensation that is not a fine, and so too is implied in [the chapter] HaSokher et HaPo'alim (Bava Metzia 91a), which I cited above. And this is surprising: for in the first chapter of Makkot (4b), Ulla states [that] the reason of Rabbi Meir — who says [that] conspiring witnesses are flogged and pay — is because he derives [it] from a defamer (motzi shem ra); and [the Gemara] asks: what [comparison can be made] to a defamer, since [the payment there] is a fine? [And it answers:] He holds like Rabbi Akiva, who says [that the payment of] conspiring witnesses is a fine. This implies that for [ordinary] monetary compensation, one is not flogged and pays! And one can answer: certainly, if [the payment of] conspiring witnesses were [ordinary] monetary compensation, he would not have derived [it] from a defamer, since [the latter] is a fine; rather, we would have expounded from [the verse] "according to his wickedness" that one is not flogged and pays. However, now that he holds [that the payment of] conspiring witnesses is a fine, and he derives from a defamer that they are flogged and pay — perforce he establishes "according to his wickedness" [as referring] to death and lashes. Since "according to his wickedness" does not refer to lashes and monetary compensation, from now on in every case one is flogged and pays, for from where would we exclude [him] so that he should not be flogged and pay?

Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:1:2.hebrew: דאמר רבה היה גדי גנוב לו - אליבא דרבי מאיר קאמר, ולא משום דסבר הכי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:1:2.english: As Rabbah said: [If] one had a stolen kid - [Rabbah] states [this] according to Rabbi Meir, and not because he [himself] holds this [view].

Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:3:1.hebrew: משום דאיסורו איסור עולם כו' - שאם חלל שבת, לאחר השבת יעידו עליו ויהרגוהו; אבל מחתרת, אע"פ שמתחייב בנפשו בעודו במחתרת, מ"מ אחר שיצא תו לא הוי בר קטלא, ולא הוי דומיא ד"אם יהיה אסון":
Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:3:1.english: "Because its prohibition is an eternal prohibition, etc." - For if one desecrated Shabbat, after Shabbat [witnesses] can testify against him and they execute him; however, [in the case of] burglary, even though he forfeits his life while he is in [the act of] burglary, nevertheless, after he has left he is no longer liable to execution, and it is not comparable to "if there shall be a fatality."

Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:3:2.hebrew: אבל שבת דבעי התראה אימא לא - תימה, דעיקר קים ליה בדרבה מיניה ברציחה כתיב, דבעינן התראה! ועוד, דשבת ומחתרת תרווייהו תננהי: דבפרק המניח (ב"ק דף לד:) תנן: "והוא שהדליק את הגדיש בשבת פטור מפני שנידון בנפשו"; ומחתרת נמי תנינא בפרק בן סורר (סנהדרין עב.): "היה בא במחתרת ושיבר את החבית, אם אין לו דמים פטור". ונראה דהכא עביד צריכותא אמאי דבקנס מיקטיל ומשלם, וה"ק: משום דחמיר איסוריה, והוה אמינא דהתם דווקא הוא דליחייב קנס עם המיתה; וכה"ג עביד צריכותא לקמן (כתובות דף לז.) גבי "לא יהיה אסון" ו"כדי רשעתו", דמשום דחמור הוי אמרינן דלעביד ביה תרתי. אבל קשה: למאי דפרישית דרבה אליבא דרבי מאיר קאמר, אם כן היכי קאמר "אבל שבת דבעיא התראה אימא לא" — מיקטיל ומשלם? והא עיקר מילתיה דרבי מאיר גבי שבת תניא לעיל! ומצינן למימר דרבה אשמועינן דשייך קים ליה בדרבה מיניה אע"ג דבשעה דמתחייב עדיין הממון בעין — לא הוה לן למימר קים לי' בדרבה מיניה, כדאמר רבה גופיה בפרק בן סורר (סנהדרין עב. ושם): "אמר רבה: מסתברא מילתיה דרב כששיבר, דליתנהו, אבל נטל, דאיתנהו — לא" — אפ"ה כיון דטבח אחרי כן מיפטר על הגנבה, ואהא דפטור אגנבה אף על גב דבאותה שעה הוי בעין עביד צריכותא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:3:2.english: However, Shabbat, which requires forewarning, say not - This is astonishing, for the primary [source of] kim leih biderabbah mineih [lit., "he stands under the greater punishment"] is written regarding murder, where we require forewarning! Furthermore, both Shabbat and burglary are taught [explicitly in Mishnayot]: for in the chapter [entitled] Hamaniach (Bava Kamma 34b) we learned: "And this is when he set fire to the stack of grain on Shabbat, he is exempt because he is judged with his life"; and [the case of] burglary we also learned in the chapter [entitled] Ben Sorer (Sanhedrin 72a): "[If] he was coming in [by] tunneling and broke the barrel, if he does not have bloodguilt, he is exempt." And it appears that here [the Gemara] makes a tzerikhuta [an explanation of why both cases are necessary] regarding [the principle] that for a fine one is executed and pays, and this is what it is saying: because its prohibition is severe, I might have thought that specifically there [in the more severe case] one should be liable for a fine together with the death penalty; and similarly, [the Gemara] makes a tzerikhuta later (Ketubot 37a) regarding "there shall not be a fatality" and "according to his wickedness," [arguing] that because it is severe we would say that we should apply both [punishments] to him. However, it is difficult: according to what I explained [earlier] that Rabbah is speaking according to Rabbi Meir, if so, how can [the Gemara] say, "However, Shabbat, which requires forewarning, say not" — [meaning] he is executed and pays? Surely the primary statement of Rabbi Meir was taught above regarding Shabbat! And we can say that Rabbah is teaching us that kim leih biderabbah mineih applies even though at the time he becomes liable [for the theft] the property is still intact — [where otherwise] we would not say kim leih biderabbah mineih, as Rabbah himself said in the chapter [entitled] Ben Sorer (Sanhedrin 72a, and there [in the sugya]): "Rabbah said: Rav's statement makes sense when he broke [the barrel], since [the pieces] are no longer [in his possession], but [if] he took [it], since it is still [in his possession] — no [he is not exempt]"; even so, since he slaughtered [the animal] afterward, he is exempt for the theft [itself], and it is regarding this [point] — that he is exempt for the theft even though at that time it was intact — that [the Gemara] makes the tzerikhuta.

Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:6:1.hebrew: מתה אין חייבין באונסין - אבל בגנבה ואבדה, נראה לר"י שהן חייבין, דהואיל ונהנין דמשתמשין בה; והכי אמר בהשואל (ב"מ צו. ושם):
Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:6:1.english: If it died, they are not liable for unavoidable accidents - However, for theft and loss, it appears to Ri that they are liable, since they derive benefit in that they use it; and so [the Gemara] states in [the chapter] HaSho'el (Bava Metzia 96a, and there).

Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:7:1.hebrew: אבל ארישא לא והיינו דרב פפא - דלא אמרינן משעת שאלה חייב באונסין. וא"ת: אם כן, בסיפא נמי בשטבחוה, אמאי משלמין כשהניח להן אביהן אחריות נכסים, הא לא נתחייב בהן האב? וי"ל: דהתם פשע בה האב, שהיה לו לומר לבניו שאינה שלו; הלכך מחיים פשע בה, ונתחייב בה באותה שעה, ונשתעבדו נכסיו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 34b:7:1.english: However, with regard to the first clause, not — and this is [consistent with the ruling] of Rav Pappa - For we do not say [that a borrower is] liable for unavoidable accidents from the time of borrowing. And if you should ask: If so, in the latter clause as well, when they slaughtered it, why do they pay when their father left them property as a guarantee — behold, the father had not become liable for them? And one can answer that there, the father was negligent with it, for he should have told his sons that it was not his; therefore, during [his] lifetime he was negligent with it, and became liable for it at that moment, and his property became encumbered [with a lien].
